sources.cite: BHEL, e-tender enquiry PSER:PUR:MJA-S670:26 (ENQ:26:PP:0015:PUR:27), 20-08-2026, overhaul of a THRI 108/44-F hydrogen-cooled 250 MW generator: a contract scope, not a maker's manual. Section B.a items 1-8 PDF pp. 28-29 (printed 7-8); B.f items 1-6 and B.g PDF p. 30 (printed 9)
WEG, Installation, operation and maintenance manual, turbogenerators, S line, horizontal, document 10174576 rev. 11: §8.1 disassembly and §8.2 assembly (the reverse), p. 46

plinth.name: Foundation block
plinth.does: The concrete block the generator stands on, in line with its turbine.

stator.name: Stator
stator.does: The frame with its laminated core and the three-phase winding in the core's slots: the rotor's turning field induces the generator's voltage in it. The end turns of the winding stand out at both ends of the core.
stator.material: Steel frame, laminated electrical steel core, copper winding

terminal_box.name: Terminal box
terminal_box.does: Under the frame: the phase and neutral terminal bushings bring the winding's ends out to the busbars.

cooler.name: Coolers
cooler.does: Water-to-air heat exchangers in their housing on top: the air the rotor's fans drive round the machine gives up its heat to the cooling water.

cw_pipes.name: Cooling water pipes
cw_pipes.does: Bring the cooling water to the coolers and take it away.

es_te_up.name: Drive-end shield, upper half
es_te_up.does: Closes the frame at the turbine end above the shaft line; its bottom half is bolted to it.

es_te_lo.name: Drive-end shield, lower half
es_te_lo.does: Closes the frame at the turbine end below the shaft line.

es_ee_up.name: Exciter-end shield, upper half
es_ee_up.does: Closes the frame at the exciter end above the shaft line.

es_ee_lo.name: Exciter-end shield, lower half
es_ee_lo.does: Closes the frame at the exciter end below the shaft line.

fan_shield_te.name: Drive-end fan shield
fan_shield_te.does: The air guide round the rotor's fan at the turbine end.

fan_shield_ee.name: Exciter-end fan shield
fan_shield_ee.does: The air guide round the rotor's fan at the exciter end.

ped_te.name: Drive-end bearing pedestal
ped_te.does: Carries the rotor's journal at the turbine end in the bearing's bottom half; insulated from the frame against shaft currents at the exciter end.
ped_te.material: Cast steel, white-metal lined bearing shell

ped_ee.name: Exciter-end bearing pedestal
ped_ee.does: Carries the rotor's journal at the exciter end in the bearing's bottom half.
ped_ee.material: Cast steel, white-metal lined bearing shell

brg_cap_te.name: Drive-end bearing top half
brg_cap_te.does: The bearing's top half and its cap with the outer oil catcher; its temperature sensor comes out first.

brg_cap_ee.name: Exciter-end bearing top half
brg_cap_ee.does: The bearing's top half and its cap with the outer oil catcher.

rotor.name: Rotor
rotor.does: One forging: its body carries the field winding in slots, held at the ends by retaining rings; a fan at each end drives the cooling air. Turned by the turbine through the coupling.
rotor.material: Alloy steel forging, copper field winding, non-magnetic steel retaining rings

exc_cover.name: Exciter hood
exc_cover.does: Encloses the exciter at the end of the shaft line.

exciter.name: Exciter
exciter.does: A brushless exciter: its stator on its bed, its rotor (the armature, the diode wheel) on the shaft's end, feeding the rotor's field without brushes.
exciter.sealed_why: The exciter comes off its bed whole, its rotor in it, once it is uncoupled.

exc_rotor.name: Exciter rotor
exc_rotor.does: The exciter's armature and diode wheel on their shaft, coupled to the generator's rotor.

coupling_bolts.name: 12 coupling bolts
coupling_bolts.beyond: The gas turbine's rotor: the next machine on the shaft line

text: The foundation block stays.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.

text: The stator stays on its foundation.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: plinth
The stator stands on the block.
The block stays.

text: Thread the rotor into the stator's bore from the drive end, its weight carried all the way.
why: It must never drag on the core or the end windings (WEG §8.1); the air gap is measured at both ends before it comes out. BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: stator
The rotor goes into the stator's bore: the stator is there first.
Thread the rotor out before the stator is touched.

text: Fit the drive-end fan shield round the rotor's fan.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: rotor
The fan shield goes round the rotor's fan: thread the rotor in first.
Take the fan shield out before the rotor is threaded out.

text: Fit the exciter-end fan shield the same way.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: rotor
The fan shield goes round the rotor's fan: thread the rotor in first.
Take the fan shield out before the rotor is threaded out.

text: Raise the drive end shield's bottom half into place under the shaft.
why: BHEL fits the bottom halves with the rotor (f.1) and lowers them just before it comes out (a.7). Its hydrogen seals and their seal oil are a hydrogen-cooled machine's: this one is air-cooled. BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: rotor
The bottom half closes under the rotor's shaft: thread the rotor in first.
Lower the bottom half before the rotor is threaded out.

text: Raise the exciter end shield's bottom half into place.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: rotor
The bottom half closes under the rotor's shaft: thread the rotor in first.
Lower the bottom half before the rotor is threaded out.

text: Set the drive-end bearing's bottom half in its pedestal under the journal and lower the rotor onto it.
why: Its clearances are recorded as it comes out and checked as it goes back (a.7, f.3, f.5). BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: rotor
The bearing carries the rotor's journal: thread the rotor in first.
Take the bearing's bottom half out, the rotor held, before the rotor is threaded out.

text: Set the exciter-end bearing's bottom half in its pedestal the same way.
why: Its pedestal is insulated: the insulation's resistance is checked once it is assembled (f.5). BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: rotor
The bearing carries the rotor's journal: thread the rotor in first.
Take the bearing's bottom half out, the rotor held, before the rotor is threaded out.

text: Align the rotor to the turbine's and fit the coupling bolts with the bolt stretcher; check the coupled run-out.
why: The coupling's run-out is recorded before it is parted (a.2). BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: ped_te
The rotor is aligned on its bearings: they are in first.
Take the coupling bolts out before the bearings are touched.

text: Lower the drive end shield's top half onto the bottom half, sealed.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: es_te_lo
The top half bolts onto the bottom half: fit that first.
Lift the top half off before the bottom half is lowered.
fan_shield_te
The end shield closes over the fan shield: fit it first.
Lift the end shield off before the fan shield comes out.

text: Lower the exciter end shield's top half onto its bottom half, sealed.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: es_ee_lo
The top half bolts onto the bottom half: fit that first.
Lift the top half off before the bottom half is lowered.
fan_shield_ee
The end shield closes over the fan shield: fit it first.
Lift the end shield off before the fan shield comes out.

text: Fit the drive-end bearing's top half and cap with its outer oil catcher; refit its temperature sensor.
why: WEG takes the bearing sensors and the grounding brush off before the bearings. BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: ped_te
The top half closes over the journal in the bottom half: fit that first.
Lift the bearing's top half off first.

text: Fit the exciter-end bearing's top half and cap the same way.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: ped_ee
The top half closes over the journal in the bottom half: fit that first.
Lift the bearing's top half off first.

text: Set the exciter on its bed, align it to the generator's rotor and couple it.
why: Its swing and run-out are recorded before it is uncoupled (a.3, g.3). BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: ped_ee
The exciter is coupled to the rotor on its bearings: they are in first.
Uncouple the exciter and take it off its bed before the exciter-end bearing is touched.

text: The exciter's rotor comes with it, coupled to the generator's.
why: BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.

text: Fit the exciter's hood.
why: The enclosures come off first of all (a.1, a.3). BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: exciter
The hood closes over the exciter: set it on its bed first.
Take the hood off first.

text: Lower the coolers into their housing on top of the frame.
why: Each cooler is pressure-tested while it is out (a.6). BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: stator
The coolers sit on the stator's frame: it is there first.
Lift the coolers off before the stator is touched.

text: Reconnect the cooling water pipes to the coolers.
why: WEG disconnects the cooling water and oil pipes before anything else. BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: cooler
The pipes feed the coolers: lower them in first.
Disconnect the cooling water pipes before the coolers are lifted.

text: Mount the phase and neutral terminal bushings with new gaskets and connect their jumpers.
why: Each bushing is pressure-tested on its own while it is out (a.1). WEG disconnects the electrical connections before the generator is opened. BHEL's overhaul scope (a contract scope, not a maker's manual) gives the order.
needs: stator
The bushings bring the stator winding's ends out: it is there first.
Disconnect the jumpers and take the bushings out first.
